events_chronological: An opening sequence relates three improbable coincidences, the last of them a boy who leaps from a rooftop and is shot on the way down by his own mother.
Television producer Ward Halbrook walked out on his dying wife and their son, who reinvented himself as the seduction guru Dean Royce.
Hal Slade, host of a long-running children's quiz show, abused his daughter Nadine, who has not spoken to him in years.
Bertie Sloan was a famous quiz-show child star whose parents kept every cent of his winnings.
Ward Halbrook, dying of cancer, is nursed at home by a male nurse called Pell while his young wife Rhoda comes apart.
Hal Slade learns he has months to live and tells his wife Beth that he cannot go on.
The quiz kid Milo is driven to another taping by a father living off him.
Nadine takes cocaine alone with the stereo at full volume, and a neighbour calls the police.
Officer Tam answers the call, is charmed by Nadine and asks her out, then loses his gun on a later call and spends the day hunting for it.
Dean Royce works a hall of men through his seminar Conquer and Discard and is then ambushed in an interview about the father he claims is dead.
Rhoda goes from lawyer to pharmacy in a rage, trying to have Ward's will changed so that she gets nothing.
Pell tracks Dean down by telephone and begs him to come and see his dying father.
Bertie, in love with a bartender, decides to steal from the office that has just sacked him.
Milo wets himself on air and refuses to answer another question, and the show collapses live.
Hal breaks down on camera and afterwards admits to Beth that he did what Nadine says he did.
Rhoda swallows her pills in the car and is found by a neighbourhood boy who takes her money before calling for help.
Dean arrives at his father's bedside and screams at the unconscious man, then weeps over him.
Hal raises a gun to his own head just as frogs begin falling out of the sky over the valley.
The rain of frogs wrecks cars across the valley and knocks Bertie off the pole he is climbing, and Tam picks him up and lets him put the money back.
Ward dies, Rhoda is taken to hospital, Milo tells his father to be nicer to him, and Nadine turns to Tam and smiles.
nonlinear_category_reason: One day holds 15 of 18 scenes and runs forward, with the prologue and two buried histories inserted from years earlier.
syuzhet_notes: Told-order bullet 1 is a self-contained prologue set decades earlier, and everything after it covers a single day, cut between nine storylines almost continuously. The nonlinearity is less a shuffled timeline than the late release of buried history: told-order bullets 4, 9 and 14 reach years behind the day the film is otherwise living in, and each arrives at the moment it does most damage.
fabula_notes: The nine strands run simultaneously through one day, so a single chronology has to impose an order on scenes the film shows as concurrent. The producer's abandonment of his first family and the host's abuse of his daughter are established through confession and archive footage rather than dramatised as they happened.
